title: Jio shares surge 21% in market debut after blockbuster India IPO

claims.claim: Jio Platforms raised $3.2 billion in India’s largest and most subscribed IPO, surging 21% in its stock market debut on Wednesday.

evidence.quote: Jio Platforms, billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Indian telecom and digital services unit backed by Meta and Google, surged 21% in its stock market debut on Wednesday after raising $3.2 billion in India’s largest and most subscribed IPO

claims.claim: The shares opened at ₹1,358 apiece, up from their IPO price of ₹1,119.

evidence.quote: The shares opened at ₹1,358 (about $14) apiece, up from their IPO price of ₹1,119 (around $12).

claims.claim: The IPO valued Jio at around ₹12.5 trillion, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries.

evidence.quote: That valued Jio at around ₹12.5 trillion (around $131.9 billion), making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after its parent, Reliance Industries

claims.claim: The offering ran from October 21 to 22 and drew bids for 22.19 times the shares on sale from more than 13.8 million people.

evidence.quote: The offering, which ran from October 21 to 22, drew bids for 22.19 times the shares on sale, according to exchange data. More than 13.8 million people applied.

claims.claim: Akash Ambani stated at the listing ceremony that Jio platforms serve more than 540 million customers.

evidence.quote: Akash Ambani (pictured above), Jio Platforms’ managing director, said at Wednesday’s listing ceremony that its platforms serve more than 540 million customers.

claims.claim: Jio made ₹300.5 billion in profit on revenue of ₹1.47 trillion in the fiscal year ended March 2026.

evidence.quote: Jio made ₹300.5 billion (about $3.2 billion) in profit on revenue of ₹1.47 trillion (around $15.5 billion) in the fiscal year ended March 2026

claims.claim: Jio plans to use up to ₹275 billion from the IPO proceeds to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.

evidence.quote: From the IPO proceeds, Jio plans to use up to ₹275 billion (about $2.9 billion) to repay debt at its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm

claims.claim: In 2020, Meta invested $5.7 billion and Google put in $4.5 billion into Jio.

evidence.quote: Meta, then known as Facebook, invested $5.7 billion, while Google put in $4.5 billion.
